title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes axiomatize a 'structure of figures' (F, ≤). Here F is a family of 'figures' (closed, stratified pieces of a tame space), ordered by inclusion. M is the poset of irreducible figures (or strata, i.e. closures of strata). A figure is identified with the set of irreducible figures below it, a down-closed subset of M. Page 58 adds a compatibility notion and axiom C3: two figures are compatible iff every pair of their members is compatible. As a corollary, a family is compatible with H iff each member is.

Page 59 draws the consequence. The whole global structure, given the poset M, reduces to one extra datum: a 'compatibility' relation R on M. R is reflexive and symmetric, so it amounts to a set S of (unordered) pairs. It is also downward hereditary: R(X,Y) implies R(X',Y') whenever X' ≤ X and Y' ≤ Y. From (M, ≤, R) one can reconstruct (F, ≤), at least on the part of finite type.

Terminology introduced:
- Irreducible components of a figure F: the maximal strata (irreducible subfigures) of F.
- Finite figure: F has finitely many strata (and F ≠ ∅_F, the empty figure).
- Figure of finite type: F is the sup of its irreducible components, and these are finite in number.
- Every finite figure is of finite type. N.B.: in the most important cases every figure is finite, hence of finite type.

Claim (completed on p.60): the set F_tf of figures of finite type is recovered from (M, ≤, R) alone. The finite-type figures are the subsets A = ∪_i M_{≤x_i}, with {x_i} a finite set of pairwise R-compatible elements.

Conversely, p.60 characterizes the abstract data, with conditions:
- (a) down-sets M_{≤x} finite, or at least every closed bounded part of finite type;
- (b) R is downward hereditary;
- figures = closed, finite-type, pairwise-compatible subsets.

In modern terms: a poset with finite principal ideals plus a reflexive symmetric downward-closed 'consistency' relation, whose 'points' are finitely generated down-closed cliques. This is exactly a prime event structure (E, ≤, #) with # the complement of R: conflict is irreflexive, symmetric and inherited upward. Figures are then its finite configurations. Equivalently, the family of figures forms a coherent (pairwise-consistency) prime-algebraic domain. Geometrically it is the stratification poset with a 'clique/flag' condition (C3 is a flag/Helly-type axiom).
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The reconstruction recovers only figures of finite type, as Grothendieck himself restricts.

Gap: passing from pairwise compatibility of the x_i to compatibility (existence of the union figure) of the whole finite family needs C3 iterated together with the corollary of p.58. This is implicit, not stated on this page.
Implicit assumption: each figure is determined by the set of irreducible figures below it, so that principal down-sets M_{≤x} represent irreducible figures. This is stated nowhere here.

ideas.what: Encoding a structure of figures by (M, ≤, R): the poset of irreducible strata plus a reflexive symmetric, downward-hereditary compatibility relation.
ideas.modern_name: Prime event structure (causality order + conflict = complement of R) / coherence (consistency) relation on a poset

ideas.what: Figures of finite type recovered as finite unions of principal down-sets M_{≤x_i} with x_i pairwise compatible.
ideas.modern_name: Finite configurations / compact elements of a coherent prime-algebraic (dI-)domain; clique (flag) complex construction

ideas.what: Irreducible components of a figure = maximal strata; figure of finite type = sup of finitely many irreducible components.
ideas.modern_name: Irreducible components in a Noetherian/stratified setting
ideas.where_published: EGA I/IV (irreducible components), in a different setting

missed.claim: Grothendieck's combinatorial encoding of tame-topological 'figures' by a poset of strata with finite down-sets and a downward-hereditary symmetric compatibility relation is literally the definition of a prime event structure. His figures are its finite configurations, and his axiom C3 (pairwise compatible ⇒ compatible) is the coherence condition of Plotkin/Girard domains. The link between stratified-space combinatorics in 'Analysis situs' and the event-structure / coherence-space semantics of concurrency and linear logic (contemporaneous, 1981-87) does not seem to have been made.
missed.quote: R(X,Y) implique R(X',Y') pour X'≤X, Y'≤Y. Cela permet ... de reconstituer (F,≤)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests that the domain-theoretic toolkit applies directly to Grothendieck's program of a tame 'analysis situs' of stratified spaces, and conversely gives geometric models of event structures. Relevant tools include stable functions, dI-domains, and the geometric realization of configuration spaces as in higher-dimensional automata.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up an elegant but elementary combinatorial reduction. Its interest is that it independently reproduces the prime event structure / coherence-space formalism in a topological context, a connection apparently not noted in the literature. No deep new result is stated.
